title: Calculating a binomial probability
problem: A fair die is rolled 4 times. Find the probability of getting exactly 2 sixes.

steps.instruction: Identify the distribution. Let $X$ = number of sixes; each roll is independent with $P(\text{six}) = \tfrac{1}{6}$.
Apply the binomial probability formula $P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k}p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$ with $n = 4$, $k = 2$, $p = \tfrac{1}{6}$.

title: Mean, variance and standard deviation
problem: $X \sim B(20, 0.35)$. Find the mean, variance and standard deviation of $X$.

steps.instruction: Find the standard deviation by taking the square root of the variance.

title: Using the complement
problem: In a clinical trial, 30% of patients respond to a new treatment. 6 patients are enrolled. Find the probability that at least 1 responds.

steps.instruction: Identify the distribution. Let $X$ = number who respond; $X \sim B(6, 0.3)$.
Use the complement $P(X \geq 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) = 1 - (1-p)^n$, which is much more efficient than summing $P(X=1) + \cdots + P(X=6)$.
